comment: Canonical pattern registry. NORMATIVE AND FROZEN: a shipped pattern's defaults never change — changing them requires a new pattern id or a major version, because specs store intent and are re-resolved on every generate. A verbatim copy lives at web/src/app/patterns.json; patterns_contract_test.go fails CI if they differ.

patterns.label: API microservice
checklist: Find the port the app actually listens on (code or Dockerfile EXPOSE) and set service.port.
Find or add the real liveness and readiness endpoints; decide whether readiness should check dependencies.
Map required env vars: which come from shared config, which need this chart's own Secret.
Measure or estimate request drain time on shutdown and set terminationGracePeriodSeconds from it.
Size resources requests and the memory limit from observed or expected load.

patterns.label: Internal gRPC service
checklist: Check whether the server registers the standard gRPC health service; if not, add it (preferred) or switch the probes to grpc_health_probe.
Decide whether server reflection should be enabled outside development.
Find configured max message sizes and document them in values comments.
Set the real listening port on service.port (scaffold default 50051).

patterns.label: Edge gateway / BFF
checklist: Wire upstream service names to sibling subcharts' Service DNS via env or config.
Extract the route table from the code and document it in the chart README.
Find per-upstream timeouts and make sure the ingress timeout exceeds the slowest of them.
This should usually be the platform's only public entry — confirm sibling subcharts don't also set ingress.

patterns.label: Web frontend
patterns.example: SPA behind nginx, Next.js app, static site
checklist: Confirm the asset base path baked into the image matches ingress.path — changing the path means a rebuild, not a values edit.
Determine SSR vs static: SSR needs env vars and a real readiness endpoint like an API service.
Define the cache-header strategy (hashed assets long-lived, HTML no-cache).

patterns.label: Job executor / queue worker
patterns.example: email sender, image resizer, Celery/Sidekiq-style consumer
checklist: Wire the queue/broker connection env vars (endpoint via config, credentials via a Secret).
Define a liveness signal for a process nobody contacts — exec heartbeat or staleness file — and set the commented livenessProbe stub.
Measure in-flight job drain time and set terminationGracePeriodSeconds from it (the most under-set value in worker charts).
Find the concurrency per pod and size the resources block from it.

patterns.label: Stream processor
patterns.example: Kafka consumer group, CDC consumer, enrichment stage
checklist: Find the consumer group id and topic(s) and wire them via config.
Set podCount.static from the partition count (replicas must stay <= partitions).
Check offset-commit semantics: is a rolling restart safe, or must maxUnavailable be tightened?
Do NOT add an HPA — autoscaling churns consumer-group rebalances.

patterns.label: Scheduler / singleton controller
patterns.example: cron dispatcher, outbox relay, leader-elected reconciler
checklist: Determine what happens if two instances ever overlap (idempotent? locked? data race?) — decide whether Recreate suffices or the app needs leader election.
Check whether this workload is really a CronJob in disguise (runs then idles); if so, flag it — chartpress doesn't generate CronJobs yet.
Do NOT raise the replica count and do NOT add an HPA or PDB.

patterns.label: Realtime gateway
patterns.example: WebSocket hub, SSE fan-out, push edge
checklist: Implement connection drain on shutdown (close frames, client retry) and set a preStop hook plus a matching grace period.
Decide whether sticky sessions are genuinely required; if so, add the controller's session-affinity annotation to ingress.annotations.
Find the max connections per pod and size resources (and the fixed replica count) from it.
Do NOT switch to CPU autoscaling — scale-downs sever long-lived connections.

patterns.label: ML inference service
patterns.example: custom model server, embedding service, LLM wrapper
checklist: Measure model load time and budget the startupProbe (periodSeconds x failureThreshold must exceed the slowest cold start).
Add GPU resource requests plus the node selector/toleration for GPU nodes if the model needs them.
Determine where the model comes from — baked into the image, init container, or volume — and wire it.

patterns.label: Webhook ingest endpoint
checklist: Wire the signature-verification secret as this chart's own Secret (not shared config).
Check the provider's payload sizes against the ingress body-size limit and raise it if needed.
Verify the handler dedupes — webhooks redeliver; idempotency is not optional.

patterns.label: Admin / back-office dashboard
checklist: PROTECT THIS ROUTE: choose the auth mechanism (SSO proxy annotations, basic-auth secret, or app-level) and add the concrete ingress annotations.
Point ingress at the internal/private ingress class if the platform has one.
Confirm the dashboard is not reachable from the public internet before calling this chart done.

patterns.label: Node agent
patterns.example: log shipper, custom node exporter, security agent
checklist: List the hostPath mounts the agent needs and why; add them to volumes.
Decide which taints it must tolerate (control-plane? dedicated pools?) and set tolerations.
Enumerate the Kubernetes API access the agent needs and hand-write a least-privilege Role/RoleBinding.

patterns.label: Custom
patterns.example: anything the twelve patterns don't fit
checklist: Set the real image registry, name, and a pinned tag.
Resolve every probe, port, and resource placeholder against the application code.
Set the security context (runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, dropped capabilities).
Measure shutdown drain time and set terminationGracePeriodSeconds.
Review scaling: pin replicas or size the HPA to match how this workload actually scales.
Enable networkPolicy with the actual callers once they're known.
